Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick post-call recap and the clarification items we promised to follow up on. Inline action items at the bottom.

Recap from today's discovery:
- Primary workload: real-time summaries + downstream classification for compliance signals (avg response length ~1k tokens).
- Expected initial monthly token volume: 0.8B – 1.2B tokens, with 3x peak multipliers during market open.
- Key constraints: p95 end-to-end latency target for 1k-token responses < 500ms, and strong reliability during market hours.

Questions we need to finalize pricing/size: (please confirm)
1) Preferred GPU type for Dedicated pool (A100-80GB / H100-80GB / other).
2) Target reserved capacity size to start (number of GPUs).
3) Throughput targets in either tokens/sec or sustained RPS and peak multipliers.
4) Target unit economics you want us to work toward (target $ / 1M tokens) and any budget ranges for committed spend.

Ballpark next steps from our side once we have the above:
- Provide committed-reserved pricing estimate (monthly) and an equivalent $/1M tokens given your projected volume and batch/cache assumptions.
- Share a capacity-sizing workbook (attached) mapping GPUs -> sustained/peak tokens/sec and expected unit costs with/without KV-caching.
- Propose a 2-week POC plan to validate throughput and latency on your busiest workload window.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm items 1–4 above.
- Marcus (me): once confirmed, I'll send a formal quote + SOW and loop in Dev Patel for the technical kickoff.

Attachments: capacity_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet with GPU sizing baseline).

Best,

Marcus — thanks for the recap, that aligns well. Answers below:

1) GPU preference: H100 80GB preferred for our production models (we run a mix of Llama-derived and custom fine-tuned weights; H100 headroom helps with mixed precision and batching).
2) Reserved capacity to start: looking at an initial pool of 8 GPUs with an option to scale to 16 within 90 days depending on observed production throughput.
3) Throughput targets: sustained 50k tokens/sec aggregate during normal trading hours, with peaks up to ~150k tokens/sec during first 30 minutes of market open. Typical concurrency ~100 active sessions. Average response size ~1k tokens, average prompt size ~200 tokens.
4) Budget/unit economics: internal target is around $500 / 1M tokens as our procurement target for committed reserved capacity. We can consider a higher blended rate early in POC but procurement wants to see a path to ~$400–$500 / 1M with reserved pricing and batching/caching optimizations.

Procurement contact: procurement@fintechco.com (Tina Lee) — I'll loop her in on the next message. Also we need SOC2 evidence as part of procurement (we already have an NDA signed).

I attached our preliminary capacity_estimate.xlsx filled with our traffic profile. Happy to jump on a sizing call with Dev Patel next week.

- Alex

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. Based on your inputs (H100, 8 GPUs initial, sustained 50k tps, peaks 150k tps, target $400–$500 / 1M tokens) here's a pragmatic next set of items and a ballpark we can use internally to scope a formal quote.

Ballpark economics (very high-level, for sizing conversations only):
- Assumptions: 8 x H100-80GB reserved, 730 hours/month, model mix with efficient batching and KV prefix caching – expected effective batching improvement ~25–35% on tokens served.
- Estimated committed monthly platform+infra cost (indicative): $225k – $320k / month for the reserved 8-GPU pool + managed control plane and 24/7 support.
- Implied unit economics range with your 0.8B–1.2B tokens/month: ~ $270 – $400 / 1M tokens. With aggressive batching and caching optimizations (and a 12–18 month commit) we can get closer to your $400 target on the low end or below.

Notes on sizing and throughput mapping:
- Typical H100 sustained decode throughput (conservative) ~6–8k tokens/sec per GPU for your model class and 1k-token responses; that gives an 8 GPU pool baseline ~48–64k tokens/sec sustained (matches your 50k target).
- Peak headroom to ~150k tokens/sec will require autoscale/burst (additional GPUs or pre-warmed burst capacity) — we can model burst pricing separately or include burst pools in the reserved contract.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf (high level pricing overview), SOC2-2024.pdf (evidence packet).

Proposed next steps:
1) I will share a formal committed-reserved quote and SOW (3–6 week lead time to provision dedicated pool by default; can compress with earlier coordination).
2) Schedule a technical sizing call: Dev Patel + your infra team to validate the throughput profile and bring a simple perf test plan (we recommend a 48-hour POC that covers market open peak).
3) Procurement: we'll include contract terms, invoicing cadence, and a path to volume discounts in the quote.

Can you confirm procurement timeline (target signature date) and whether a 2/3 month pilot with a mid-term commitment is acceptable? If so, we'll put together two options: (A) 8-GPU committed + burst pool; (B) 12-GPU committed (preferred pricing) — both with explicit $/1M token equivalents for comparison.

I'll schedule a follow-up call for next week. Laura — looping you for commercial/discount questions. Dev — please prepare a short perf/POC checklist for the call.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
